newsitem.title: LATVIA: KALEV EYES FIVE PERCENT OF LATVIAN SWEETS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: KALEV EYES FIVE PERCENT OF LATVIAN SWEETS MARKET.

text.p: Kalev, the biggest Estonian confectionery maker, is aiming for five percent of Latvia's sweets market and plans to open a rep office in autumn, the Diena bizness newspaper said on Thursday.
"Kalev hopes to achieve some five percent of the market and open its rep office in Latvia in autumn," Juhan Mats, Kalev's deputy marketing manager, is quoted as saying.
"Competition between Baltic producers is unnecessary as people are mostly buying local produce," Mats is said in an interview.
Kalev's prices are slightly lower than that of Latvian and Lithuanian confectionery products, Mats said.

Chocolate is Kalev's main product, comprising 70 percent of its total production volume, which last year was 11,106 tonnes. Some 49 percent was sold in Estonia in 1996 and 44 percent was exported to Russia, the newspaper writes.
Kalev earlier acquired a 25 percent stake in Lithuania's Vilniaus Pergale and a 50 percent share ib Russia's Bogatirj, with the aim of creating an international firm.
